source.name: Copernicus Sentinel-2 L2A via Element84 Earth Search (STAC) and the Sentinel-2 COGs on AWS Open Data
source.license: Copernicus Sentinel data, free and open (contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data)

method: Window: 150 m radius around the pin (about 706 pixels of 10 m). Per quarter, newest first: up to 2 scenes from the most frequent MGRS tile that see at least 90% of the window without cloud (Sentinel-2 scene classification: vegetation, bare and water kept; cloud, cirrus, shadow, dark and unclassified removed), at most 6 cloud masks read per quarter, per-pixel median. Change between consecutive clear quarters: share of pixels seen in both whose true-colour brightness moved by more than 25 of 255, or that switched between built-up or bare (NDBI > 0 and NDVI < 0.25) and not, with NDBI moving more than 0.1, after subtracting the median change in a ring 300 to 600 m from the pin (sun angle, haze and season move the whole scene). A pair at or above 10% counts as visible change. no_visible_change_months: months between the middle of the newest clear quarter and the oldest quarter reached without visible change.
limits: 10 m pixels see slabs, roofs, cleared ground and cranes, not work inside a building: a site where only interiors are being fitted out looks unchanged, and a finished building should look unchanged. Season, sun angle, haze and wet ground also move brightness, which is why the threshold is high and the result is a prompt to ask, not a verdict. Coordinates come from public sources (about 100 m), so the window can miss part of a large site or include a neighbour.
